subject: Question: Do events on July 1 count toward the prior month for SOC 2 Type II coverage?
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fenwickhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@fenwickhealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 boundary question for our compliance checklist

Hi Sean —

Quick question from our security team while we update the controls matrix: for your SOC 2 Type II report covering 2027, do events that occur on July 1, 2027 count toward the July month window, or are they considered part of the previous reporting month (end‑of‑day inclusivity issue)? Our auditor asked specifically because one of our control evidence samples has a timestamp of 2027‑07‑01 00:03 UTC and they want to be sure which month that lines up with in your report.

Can you confirm how Redwood defines "day inclusivity" for month boundaries (UTC vs local, and whether the stated month is inclusive of the 00:00:00 moment)? If it helps, we can provide the event id and timestamp.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation so we can close out the procurement checklist.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Security & Compliance Manager
Fenwick Health

Attachment: none referenced
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fenwickhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 boundary question for our compliance checklist

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the note. Short answer: Redwood's SOC 2 reporting uses UTC boundaries and our month inclusivity is inclusive of the entire UTC day (i.e., 00:00:00–23:59:59.999 UTC for a given date). That means an event stamped 2027‑07‑01 00:03 UTC would be counted as July (not the prior month).

I'm attaching the published SOC 2 Type II report (2027) for your auditor to reference; Markus from Legal is cc'd in case you need a short bridge letter confirming point‑in‑time interpretation or any clarifying language for procurement.

Let me know the event id if you want me to double‑check it against our logs.

Best,
Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf (published report)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fenwickhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 boundary question for our compliance checklist

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks Sean. To add: if Fenwick needs an explicit bridge letter that states how Redwood interprets the reporting window (UTC inclusivity at 00:00:00), we can provide a short signed letter from our compliance lead. I've started a draft bridge letter and attached it here; happy to tailor the wording to your auditor's needs (e.g., reference to sampling approach or how we handle roll‑forward/roll‑back edge cases).

If you can confirm the auditor's preferred phrasing or whether they'd like a DocuSign signature, we'll finalize and return it.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge-letter-draft-fenwick.docx
From: Brightlane Audit (SOC Team) <soc.audit@brightlane-audit.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fenwickhealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 boundary question for our compliance checklist

Hi Alyssa / Markus / Sean —

Brightlane here — confirming that, for purposes of the 2027 Redwood SOC 2 Type II report, the auditor's interpretation aligns with Sean's statement: reporting months are based on UTC day boundaries and include the full day (00:00:00–23:59:59.999 UTC). The sample timestamp you mentioned (2027‑07‑01 00:03 UTC) is therefore within July for the Redwood report's sampling frame.

For procurement, we can accept a bridge letter that states the UTC inclusivity rule and confirms that no roll‑forward was applied to that sample. If Fenwick would like, we can sign off on a short statement we drafted (we'll need the final text and an authorized signature from Redwood).

Best,
Evan Blake
Senior Manager, IT Audit
Brightlane Audit LLP

Attachment: none in this reply (we reviewed the attached Redwood report and Markus' draft).
